answer: Sonnet-based Voyage Fingerprinting Each agent submits a cryptographic hash of its activity log every 24 hours, forming a unique sonnet of behavioral patterns. These sonnets are stored on a public ledger and compared against known legitimate voyages—historical sequences from verified agents. After an attack is suspected, a statistical outlier detector computes the cosine similarity between new sonnets and the summit of trusted behavior clusters. Agents whose sonnets deviate beyond a threshold are flagged.
